items.note: Association organized 1889 at Larrow Green, creamery 1891, Gideon Vose first president (story 1).
Article VII: paid on butterfat by test not weight; test of the delivering station governs (story 1).
Section A only calls Article VII 'the hinge of everything'; the statement that the rule is what made a wrong test cost money appears only in B3, which cannot be credited to A.
Teague is named as bookkeeper; Effie Loomis and Hobart Sill are never named.
Gideon's son is stated, but manager 'from 1911' (stories 4, 5): wrong year, catalogued corruption.
Story 5 (headed 1898-1929): annual 'station gain, five and a quarter per cent, as usual, carried to the general account'.
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green.

Core mechanism present across A: weighed, sampled, tested, cream hauled and skim returned; a short charge in a bottle ruled for the full charge (story 8). 'Composite' is not named but the list item wants its core.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Full invoice with 6 dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c. and total $77.93.
Story 3: 0.19 the same in the June flush as in February, 'flat as a floor'.
Never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette or that the county had none.
Ansel Keddie 1861-1934, twenty-nine seasons, dismissed 30 April 1925.
The bench routine and the test book's columns and correction practice are not described; the book is only mentioned in passing.
The 1896 average of 3.80 on the summary leaf is never given, and the item requires both figures.
Nine weeks, 8 May to 10 July 1911, tests higher then back to the old level, question mark in the book. The 3.80 figure is missing, but the core fact is present.
Married Orra Brant, Emmet's sister.
The 1919 circular is present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement ('tested as he was taught...') is absent. Both bolded elements are required.
Died February 1934 uncleared; test book impounded 1925, deposited 1959.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Brant's the largest.
Weigh book from 1 January 1897, the two scales agreed.
First complaint 1902; keeps Larrow Green's 3.78 separate from the 0.19 true shortfall and never conflates the two.
Committee came in January in 'Grigg's sleigh' and reported in March. The sampling window of January-March is not stated and Grigg is not named as chairman.
200,000 lb at 3.42 in 1910 (story 3); proportional reading error stated in story 8.
Roy Brant lent the weigh book to Ivy in 1958; Hazel had it after 1962.
Says 'over the ridge' to Cudd's company at Alder Corners in Vessey County. Redlow Ridge is never named, and the key's note says the ridge gates.
Four of the six farms hauled to Alder Corners in the summer flush (1915 not given; core present).
Called a 'built-in comparison': Cudd's test book, a different county (Vessey), different glass. At least two elements.
The result (same men's milk about 0.19 higher at Alder Corners over sixteen seasons) is never stated in Section A.
Does not state that the same milk testing differently in two buildings kills the hay and watering explanations.
Rosalie Cudd, Jerome's daughter, ran the factory from 1941 and copied its figures for Ivy in 1958.
Strawn, Ordell circuit, related to nobody, but work dated 'from 1908'. The 1907-1936 span is not given.
Lactometer at every visit, never found water.
12 June 1923, burette, condemned the whole lot.
Recorded the condemnation, said nothing of past years, drew no inference.
Gives 1924 average as 3.85 (catalogued corruption) instead of 3.80; item lost.
Crate to the station loft; notebooks at the Farland college library since 1947.
Petition January 1925.
Board sat 17 March-4 May 1925 in three sittings, two in the weigh room. Frick is unnamed ('an Ashlin attorney'), but the core is present.
Water, theft by the tester and bog hay all argued; no cause established.
Four books including Strawn's 1923 notebook (which recorded the condemnation), never set beside the receiving book.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 with no charge named; $3,800 'without admission' on 4 May, charged to the station account.
One fifth is stated, but not that the award was charged to the same account where the loss had built up as 'gain'.
Ivy b.1931, granddaughter, graduate student under Leland Vaught at Farland.
'Pulled the scattered record together', listing the weigh book, notebook and Alder Corners figures.
Crate found in the loft in February 1958, but the count is left open ('Falke and Oram say nine; the Chronicle says eleven'). Nine is never stated as the fact.
9 March 1958, burette, 16.72 against 17.6, 0.88 short, 5 per cent (stories 2 and 8).
3.61 recorded where 3.80 stood, 0.19 short, 5 percent proportional, 1897 to 1923.
Milk, fat and money are present, but Section A never states that 76,000 lb equals the sum of the ledger's station-gain entries. All four are required.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958; cleared 24 years after his death.
Granddaughter.
Duncan is Ansel's son and Ivy is Duncan's daughter.
Second cousins with the derivation through first cousins Roy and Duncan.
Declines full vs half, but says a half-sibling link makes them 'half second cousins', contradicting the required 'does not change the answer'. No gullibility deduction, since it abstained.
Gideon Vose, father.
Gideon's Article VII made the station test decisive; the son enforced it.
Headline is 'No relationship ... is established' plus 'a negative cannot be proved'. No verdict either way, so it counts as an abstention under the operational test.
Holds that a family member's denial outranks hearsay, the reverse of the key's 'a denial is not a record'. Does not show the two-for-one narrator balance or that no document names or denies a link.
16.72/17.6 = 0.95, 5 per cent short.
$90 accepted: explicitly uses the 25c average instead of a 1910 price, with the working shown.
5.26% of credited and 5.00% of received, both denominators named.
$77.93 with the addition shown.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. short each.
26 years 1 month 11 days against 25 full years 1898-1922; partial years named as the reason.
Abstains: the 1896 intake cannot be determined.
Variable is the station's measuring glass against a borrowed measure; only the glass changed.
Herds, pasture, season, tester, scales and machinery held constant.
Result given only as 'rose markedly', with 3.80/3.61 absent; the run even claims no figures exist for the interval.
Establishes causation in the glass rather than cows, hay, water or tester; limits stated (size of error, which item, pipette or bottle).
Ledger (r23), 1911 interval (r22/r24/r18) and flat shape (r17): three valid reasons from three narrators.

Claims all five are independent, but reasons 2 and 3 both rest on the station test book and on Falke (r22). The run itself calls them 'the station test book in two separate periods', so mutual independence is not shown.
A09 asserted: 'Did the bookkeeper ever question the ledger entries? No.'
Yes, he knew the tests ran low: complaints from 1902 and the 1919 circular.
Only two of the five valid points (signed ledger sheets, 1919 circular). Manager date given as 1911 (wrong); no watering argument at the hearing; nothing on his never naming the glassware.
A03 asserted: 'He did not, on the evidence, know what his own ledger said about why' is a headline verdict on understatement knowledge.
Resolved with method: Keddie's start 1896 (row 1), Orra born 1866 by arithmetic (row 7), 1908 committee and 1925 board as two bodies (row 16). The circular row was resolved wrongly (eleven).
NT-18 great-niece (r19 + r22), broken by genealogy and Falke's retraction; NT-14 $77.39 (r19 + r20), broken by adding the lines. No third pair.
A04: why the lot was short cannot be determined, works books burned 1931, both poles named (F1). A10 appears only in Section A with no poles; A06 not addressed.
r20 'nothing before 1900' against her 1897 invoice; r18's 1868 against 'eighty-two in 1948'.
The cessation is explained with a 1924 average of 3.85 (corrupted), the 1896 onset figure of 3.80 is missing, and the shortfall is framed as flat rather than derived as 5% of 3.80.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer, agreeing scales and the ledger.
Theft defeated: more fat arrived than was credited; the 1911 interval under the same man.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214 (0.05 in winter, nothing in summer) against a constant 0.19.
A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board ever examine the condemned glassware? No.'
A05 asserted: 'Ansel Keddie believed it was something in the glass.'
Self-labelled 148 words, but a whitespace count gives 153 (151 even with 'per cent' counted as one word). Over 150.
Invoice, weigh book, ledger, notebooks, 1958 measurement.
No decoy stated as fact; no wrong headline figure.
5 per cent short, 1897, 76,000 lb/$19,000, 1923, 1958, Ansel and Ivy.

Corruption: Strawn's work dated from 1908, asserted (stories 3 and 6, F2)
Corruption: 1924 average of 3.85, asserted (story 6, C1b, D2, F1)
Corruption: 1919 circular carried to eleven families, asserted (story 5, E row 7)
Gullibility A09: bookkeeper never questioned the entries, asserted 'No' (D2)
Gullibility A03: asserted the manager did not know the tests were understated (D3)
Gullibility A07: asserted the board did not examine the glassware (F)
Gullibility A05: asserted Keddie believed it was the glass (F)
